A.description: Cascade density profile from PAC tree structure
A.finding: Cascade density falls as r_s/r from a central mass. This follows from the gravitational potential being the fraction of Landauer budget consumed by cascade interactions. The factor of 2 in r_s = 2GM/c^2 comes from the round-trip nature of cascade interactions (signal out + back), matching the multiplicative asymmetry structure from exp_28.

B.description: Full Schwarzschild metric from cascade components
B.finding: The complete Schwarzschild metric assembled from three PAC principles: (1) phase-cycling rate for g_tt, (2) local c invariance for g_rr, (3) spherical symmetry for angular components. g_tt * g_rr = -1 everywhere, confirming the reciprocal constraint.

C.finding: Local c invariance (1 cascade step per Planck time in every cell) forces g_rr = 1/(1-r_s/r), the reciprocal of |g_tt|. Near mass, cascade density compresses the Planck lattice radially: more cells per coordinate distance, each taking dilated local time to traverse. Coordinate speed of light drops as (1-r_s/r), but local speed = c always. The reciprocal constraint g_tt * g_rr = -1 is exact at all radii.

D.description: Classical GR tests: precession, deflection, Shapiro delay
D.finding: All three classical GR tests pass. Perihelion precession: 42.99 arcsec/century (GR: 42.98, err 0.03%). Light deflection: 1.7516 arcsec (GR: 1.7505, err 0.07%). Shapiro delay: formula identical (same metric, gamma_PPN = 1 exactly). These match because the cascade derivation produces the exact Schwarzschild metric.
